```{r}
# ==============================
# Optimaler Analyse-Workflow: Moderierte Mediation
# ==============================

# 0) Packages installieren/laden ---------------------------------------------
library(dplyr)
library(car)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)
library(interactions)
library(jtools)
library(lavaan)
library(semTools)
library(stargazer)

# 1) Daten simulieren & randomisieren ----------------------------------------
set.seed(2025)
n   <- 100
IV  <- rnorm(n)
W   <- rnorm(n)
M   <- 0.5*IV + 0.3*W + 0.4*(IV*W) + rnorm(n, sd=1)
DV  <- 0.7*M  + 0.2*IV           + rnorm(n, sd=1)
df  <- data.frame(IV, W, M, DV) %>%
  slice(sample(1:n(), n())) %>%  # zufällige Reihenfolge
  mutate(id = row_number()) %>%
  select(id, everything())

# 2) Variablen zentrieren & Interaktionsterm --------------------------------
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    IV_c = scale(IV, center=TRUE, scale=FALSE),
    W_c  = scale(W,  center=TRUE, scale=FALSE),
    Int  = IV_c * W_c
  )

# 3) Basis-Modell (Total-Effekt c) -------------------------------------------
fit_total <- lm(DV ~ IV_c, data = df)

# 4) Mediations- & Moderationsmodelle ---------------------------------------
## 4.1 a-Pfad mit Moderation (M ~ IV + W + IV×W)
fit_a <- lm(M ~ IV_c * W_c, data = df)

## 4.2 b- & c′-Pfad (DV ~ M + IV + W)
fit_b <- lm(DV ~ M + IV_c + W_c, data = df)

# 5) Robuste Standardfehler (HC3) --------------------------------------------
se_total <- sqrt(diag(vcovHC(fit_total, type="HC3")))
se_a     <- sqrt(diag(vcovHC(fit_a,     type="HC3")))
se_b     <- sqrt(diag(vcovHC(fit_b,     type="HC3")))

# 6) Subgruppen-Analysen (±1 SD von W_c) -------------------------------------
sd_w    <- sd(df$W_c)
df_low  <- filter(df, W_c <= -sd_w)
df_high <- filter(df, W_c >=  sd_w)

fit_low  <- lm(M ~ IV_c, data = df_low)
fit_high <- lm(M ~ IV_c, data = df_high)

# 7) Simple Slopes & Johnson–Neyman ------------------------------------------
interact_plot(fit_a, pred = IV_c, modx = W_c,
              interval=TRUE, int.width=0.95)
johnson_neyman(fit_a, pred="IV_c", modx="W_c", alpha=0.05)

# 8) SEM mit Bootstrapping (bedingte indirekte Effekte) ----------------------
sem_model <- '
  # a-Pfad mit Moderation
  M  ~ a1*IV_c + a2*W_c + a3*Int
  # b-Pfad + direkter c′-Effekt
  DV ~ b*M + c*IV_c + d*W_c

  # bedingte indirekte Effekte bei W = –1 SD / +1 SD
  IE_low  := (a1 + a3*(-1)) * b
  IE_high := (a1 + a3*( 1)) * b
'
fit_sem <- sem(sem_model,
               data          = df,
               se            = "bootstrap",
               bootstrap     = 5000,
               meanstructure = TRUE)

# 9) SEM-Ergebnisse (CI & Standardisiert) -----------------------------------
summary(fit_sem,
        standardized = TRUE,
        ci           = TRUE,
        rsquare      = TRUE)

# 10) stargazer-Output für’s Paper -------------------------------------------
stargazer(
  # Modelle
  fit_total, fit_a, fit_b, fit_low, fit_high,
  # Robuste SEs
  se            = list(se_total, se_a, se_b, NULL, NULL),
  # Beschriftungen
  title           = "Übersicht der Regressionsmodelle: Moderierte Mediation",
  column.labels   = c("Total-Effekt", "a-Pfad gesamt", "b/c′-Pfad",
                      "a-Pfad (low W)", "a-Pfad (high W)"),
  dep.var.labels  = c("DV", "Mediator (M)", "DV",
                      "Mediator (M)", "Mediator (M)"),
  covariate.labels= c("IV (z)", "W (z)", "IV×W", "Mediator"),
  # LaTeX-Format
  type            = "latex",
  style           = "ajps",
  star.cutoffs    = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001),
  digits          = 3,
  align           = TRUE,
  intercept.bottom= FALSE,
  no.space        = TRUE,
  out             = "mod_med_overview.tex"
)
```

```{r}
# ================================================
# Moderierte Mediation inkl. Baseline- und Vollmodelle
# Mit Beispiel-Datensatz zum direkten Ausprobieren
# ================================================

# 0. Pakete installieren & laden (einmalig) -------------------------------
# install.packages(c("dplyr", "stargazer"))
library(dplyr)
library(stargazer)
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Datensatz laden
setwd("~/Projects/Master-Thesis-Spatial-Proximity-Venture-Capital")
data <- read_csv("data/sets-for-r/regression_data.csv")

```



```{r}
library(splines)
library(stargazer)
library(pscl)

# Knotendefinition (Median deiner Funding‐Variable)
kn <- median(data$total_seed_funding_m, na.rm=TRUE)

# Liste aller Prädiktoren – hier mit einem Splines‐Term für total_seed_funding_m
ivs <- c(
  "seed_investors_all_same_country",sprintf("bs(total_seed_funding_m, knots = %f, degree = 2, intercept = FALSE)", kn),
  "number_of_founders",
  "age",
  "headquarters_country", "hub_binary", "b2b_binary",
  "energy", "materials", "industrials", "consumer_discretionary",
  "consumer_staples", "health_care", "financials",
  "information_technology", "communication_services",
  "utilities", "real_estate", "other"
)

# Formel konstruieren und Modell schätzen
dv <- "exit_binary"
logit_formula <- reformulate(ivs, dv)
model_logit   <- glm(logit_formula, data = data, family = binomial)

# Pseudo-R²
pr2 <- pR2(model_logit)["McFadden"]

# Ausgabe mit stargazer
stargazer(
  model_logit,
  type                   = "text",
  title                  = "Logistische Regression mit Splines",
  dep.var.labels.include = FALSE,
  star.cutoffs           = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001),
  signif.stars           = TRUE,
  report                 = "vc*p",
  digits                 = 3,
  omit.stat              = c("aic", "ll"),
  add.lines              = list(
    c("McFadden’s Pseudo-R²", formatC(pr2, digits = 3))
  )
)
```

```{r}
library(splines)
library(stargazer)

# Knotendefinition (Median deiner Funding‐Variable)
kn <- median(data$total_seed_funding_m, na.rm=TRUE)

# 1) Liste aller Prädiktoren (ohne Splines, da wir hier eine lineare Regression wollen)
ivs <- c(
  "homecountry_pca_component", sprintf("bs(total_seed_funding_m, knots = %f, degree = 3, intercept = FALSE)", kn),
  "number_of_founders", "number_seed_investors",
  "age",
  "headquarters_country", "hub_binary", "b2b_binary",
  "energy", "materials", "industrials", "consumer_discretionary",
  "consumer_staples", "health_care", "financials",
  "information_technology", "communication_services",
  "utilities", "real_estate", "other"
)

# 2) Abhängige Variable definieren
dv <- "years_to_exit"

# 3) Formel konstruieren und Modell schätzen
lm_formula <- reformulate(ivs, dv)
model_lm   <- lm(lm_formula, data = data)

# 4) R² extrahieren
R2 <- summary(model_lm)$r.squared

# 5) Ausgabe mit stargazer
stargazer(
  model_lm,
  type             = "text",
  title            = "Lineare Regression",
  dep.var.labels = "Years to Exit",
  star.cutoffs   = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001),
  signif.stars   = TRUE,
  report         = "vcsp",    # v=Koeff, c=SE, s=Sterne, p=p-Werte
  digits         = 3,
  omit.stat      = c("AIC", "BIC"),
  add.lines      = list(
    c("R-squared", formatC(R2, digits = 3))
  )
)
```
